svg.title: A zero signed integral can represent nonzero geometric area
svg.desc: The line y equals x minus one crosses the x-axis at one. Between zero and one its triangular region has area one half below the axis; between one and two it has area one half above. The signed integral from zero to two is negative one half plus one half, which is zero. The total geometric area is one. Splitting at the crossing and reversing the negative integrand produces two positive contributions. Taking only the absolute value of the final signed integral incorrectly gives zero.
